title: Spider‑Man: Brand New Day Shatters Record as North American Top‑Grossing Film
text:
Sony's Spider‑Man movie has become the highest‑grossing domestic release ever, surpassing Star Wars, amassing $936.773 million in North America and $2.45 billion globally, while its chairman anticipates record‑setting domestic gains.
Springtime nostalgia meets blockbuster ambition as Sony's latest Spider‑Man feature becomes the highest‑grossing film ever released in North America. Over the course of seven weeks, the film has accumulated more than 936.773 million dollars domestically, eclipsing the former record set by Star Wars: The Force Awakens with 936 million dollars.
Fans and critics alike have marveled at the movie's trajectory, noting that it surpassed 1 billion global dollars in just six days and has already attracted $2.45 billion worldwide, positioning it only behind Avatar and Avengers: Endgame in the all‑time box office hierarchy. The momentum behind this achievement has sparked enthusiasm from Sony's top management.
Chairman Tom Rothman, speaking with Variety at the Resident Evil Fantastic Fest premiere, admitted that he never expected a post‑COVID film to generate a $300‑million opening weekend. He recalled, "I never imagined any movie could open over $300 million in the post‑COVID era.
" When asked whether the film could cross the elusive $1 billion domestic threshold, Rothman remained measured. He expressed confidence that the film would soon claim the title of the highest‑grossing North American release, but did not commit to the $1‑billion milestone. The release's current trajectory, however, shows it still needs roughly $63 million more in domestic theaters to reach that number, a target that would likely require a theatrical re‑release.
Dropping off the number one spot after six consecutive weekends, Spider‑Man: Brand New Day is now number two behind a Warner Bros. title. Its opening day alone drew $169.84 million, while the opening weekend yielded a record‑breaking $360 million. From a global perspective, the film has climbed to the third position, only surpassed by Avatar and Avengers: Endgame.
These figures underscore Sony's ability to deliver cinematic experiences that captivate audiences worldwide, and signal a robust resurgence for blockbuster franchises in an industry still adjusting to the pandemic's aftershocks. As the quest for new milestones continues, the film's performance remains a benchmark for future releases and a testament to the enduring appeal of the Spider‑Man brand
